title: Malta Year 8 Math Unit 1 — Number System Recap
question: Can powers, the LCM of three numbers, square and cube roots, and recurring decimals be applied in eight recap questions, two for each subtopic?
intro: Two questions for each subtopic, 1-1 to 1-4. **Show your method before choosing A–D.**

questions.title: 1-1 · Value of a power
questions.solution:
\[4^3 = 4\times4\times4 = \boxed{64}\]

12 multiplies the base by the exponent; 81 is \(3^4\), with base and exponent swapped; 16 is \(4^2\).

questions.title: 1-1 · Powers in BIDMAS
questions.solution:
\[5 + 2\times27 = 5 + 54 = \boxed{59}\]

189 adds first, \((5 + 2)\times27\); 221 cubes \(2\times3\) first; 23 reads \(3^3\) as 9.

questions.title: 1-2 · LCM of three numbers
questions.prompt: What is the LCM of 6, 10 and 15?
questions.solution_title: Every prime at its highest power
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} 6 &= 2\times3 \\ 10 &= 2\times5 \\ 15 &= 3\times5 \end{aligned}\]

\[\text{LCM} = 2\times3\times5 = \boxed{30}\]

60 is a common multiple but not the lowest; 900 is the product \(6\times10\times15\); 15 is not a multiple of 6.

questions.title: 1-2 · Lights flashing together
questions.prompt: Three lights flash every 4, 6 and 10 seconds. They flash together now. After how many seconds do they next flash together?
questions.solution:
\[\begin{aligned} 4 &= 2^2 \\ 6 &= 2\times3 \\ 10 &= 2\times5 \end{aligned}\]

\[\text{LCM} = 2^2\times3\times5 = \boxed{60}\]

20 adds the times; 240 is the product \(4\times6\times10\); 120 is a common multiple, but 60 comes first.

questions.title: 1-3 · Square and cube roots
questions.solution_title: Undo the square and the cube
questions.solution:
\(15\times15 = 225\) and \(7\times7\times7 = 343\), so the pair is 15 and 7.

112.5 halves 225 — a root is not a division by 2; 49 is \(7^2\), not the cube root.

questions.title: 1-3 · Estimating a root
questions.prompt: Between which two whole numbers does \(\sqrt{90}\) lie?
questions.solution:
\[81 < 90 < 100 \quad\Rightarrow\quad 9 < \sqrt{90} < 10\]

44 and 46 sit around \(90\div2 = 45\) — halving is not taking a root.

questions.title: 1-4 · Terminating or recurring
questions.prompt: Which fraction gives a recurring decimal?
questions.solution_title: A prime factor other than 2 or 5
questions.solution:
\(\frac{5}{12}\) is in simplest form and \(12 = 2^2\times3\); the 3 makes it recur: \(\frac{5}{12} = 0.41\dot{6}\).

The others terminate: \(\frac38 = 0.375\), \(\frac{7}{25} = 0.28\), \(\frac{9}{20} = 0.45\).

questions.title: 1-4 · Recurring decimal to fraction
questions.prompt: Which fraction is exactly equal to \(0.\dot{5}\)?

takeaway: A power repeats multiplication, an LCM takes every prime at its highest power, a root undoes a power, and a fraction in simplest form terminates only when its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5.
